title: Shivaji Sends Back the Governor's Daughter-in-Law
text:
Shivaji Bhosale, founder of the Maratha state in western India, spent his early career seizing forts and towns from the Sultanate of Bijapur. Maratha tradition tells of an episode from around 1657, when his commander Abaji Sondev captured the wealthy town of Kalyan, near modern Mumbai.

Among the spoils, the story goes, the commander brought back the young and beautiful daughter-in-law of the defeated governor, and presented her to Shivaji as a prize, expecting to please him.

Shivaji was angry with his officer. In the best known version he looked at the frightened woman and said that if his own mother had been as beautiful as she was, he too would have been handsome. He addressed her as a mother, gave her clothes and gifts, and had her escorted back to her family with full honor. He also made it a rule that women captured in war were not to be harmed.

The story is told in Maharashtra to this day as an example of Shivaji's respect for women, including the women of his enemies, and it is often shown in plays and paintings.
lesson: How you treat the defenseless among your opponents reveals your real character. Power over someone is a test, not a prize.
source: Maratha tradition and later bakhar chronicles
caveat: The episode comes from later tradition and is not confirmed by contemporary records, though Shivaji's orders protecting women are mentioned by other sources.
